Find the $x$-intercepts of the circle $(x-4)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}=10,$ shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We must have $y=0$ at the $x$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2}+(y+2)^{2} & =10 \\ (x-4)^{2}+(0+2)^{2} & =10 \\ (x-4)^{2}+4 & =10 \\ (x-4)^{2} & =6 \\ x-4 & =\pm \sqrt{6} \\ x & =4\pm \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts occur at the points $(4-\sqrt{6},0)$ and $(4+\sqrt{6},0).$
